ins_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me determine which insurance coverage types my startup actually needs before we request quotes for D&O, E&O, general liability, and cyber insurance. Please ask me for any of the following you don't already have: my company name and website domain, industry/business model, number of employees, whether we have outside investors or a board of directors, whether we handle or store customer/personal data, whether we sell software/services under contracts with clients (especially any contracts that mandate specific insurance minimums), whether we have a physical office or meet clients/vendors in person, our approximate annual revenue, states/countries where we operate, and any existing insurance policies we already hold.

Using that information, research and reason through which of the four coverage types are relevant and why, for example: D&O if we have a board/investors or are raising funding; E&O (professional liability) if we deliver services or software with performance obligations; general liability if we have offices, in-person meetings, or physical products; cyber if we collect/store sensitive data or offer SaaS. Note any coverage explicitly required by investor term sheets, customer contracts, or landlord leases if I mention them.

Produce a short written summary listing each of the four coverage types, whether it's needed (yes/no/maybe), the reasoning, and an estimated coverage amount range if commonly referenced for companies our size/industry (note this is a rough estimate, not a quote). Do not contact any insurers or request actual quotes — this step is only about determining requirements. Report back the summary in plain text, flagging any input I didn't provide that limited your analysis.

ins_001:n2.prompt: You are helping me prepare for the 'Get insurance quotes' process by compiling the company information packet needed for D&O, E&O, general liability, and cyber insurance applications. If you don't already have them, ask me for: legal company name, DBA (if any), incorporation state/date, entity type, principal business address, website domain, industry/NAICS code, number of employees, annual revenue (current and projected), total funding raised and from whom, names/titles of officers and directors, ownership percentages of major shareholders, prior insurance history (carrier, coverage type, limits, expiration), any prior claims or lawsuits, description of products/services offered, data types handled (e.g., PII, payment data, health data) and approximate volume, and existing security practices (encryption, access controls, incident response plan) for the cyber section. Use your configured credentials to pull any of this data from connected systems (e.g., cap table tool, HR system, domain registrar) where possible instead of asking me to retype it. Organize everything into a single structured document (Google Doc, Notion page, or Markdown file) with clear headers for: Company Overview, Financials, Leadership & Ownership, Insurance History & Claims, Product/Service Description, and Data & Security Practices (for cyber). Flag any fields you could not fill in with '[NEEDS INPUT]' so I can complete them later. Done looks like a single shareable document containing all sections above, ready to be copied into broker or carrier application forms. Report back with the document link/location, a bullet list of any '[NEEDS INPUT]' gaps, and a one-line summary confirming the packet is ready for the next quoting step.

ins_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare insurance quote applications with Embroker for D&O, E&O, general liability, and cyber insurance. This is a preparation-only task — an officer of the company must review and certify the factual representations before anything is submitted, so you must stop short of submitting.

First, ask me for any of the following you don't already have: our legal company name, domain, entity type and state of incorporation, date founded, number of employees, annual revenue or funding raised, industry/business description, prior claims history (if any), current or prior insurance carriers, key officer names/titles, and any existing security or compliance certifications (for cyber coverage). If Embroker's application requires other standard details (e.g., payroll figures, tech stack, data handled), ask me for those too.

Using your configured credentials, log into Embroker and locate the application forms for each of the four coverage lines. Fill in each form with the information I provide, leaving any field blank (and flagged clearly) if I haven't supplied the data. Do not click submit or finalize any form.

When done, prepare a summary report listing: (1) each of the four applications and its completion status, (2) all fields populated with the values used, (3) any fields left blank or uncertain that need my input, and (4) a checklist of the factual representations that require officer certification before submission.

Present this summary and stop for human sign-off — do not submit, certify, or approve any application on my behalf.

ins_001:n4.prompt:
You are helping me track the status of insurance quotes I've requested from Embroker for D&O, E&O, general liability, and cyber insurance. The quotes are expected to take 3-5 business days to arrive, and waiting on Embroker's brokers/underwriters to return these quotes remains a human step that you cannot perform or accelerate.

Before starting, ask me for: (1) the date I submitted the insurance application/request to Embroker, (2) the email address or account associated with my Embroker submission, and (3) whether I have access to my email inbox or Embroker account for you to check (if you have tool access to either).

Your job for this step is limited to preparation and monitoring support:
1. Calculate and tell me the expected quote delivery window (submission date + 3 to 5 business days).
2. If you have access to my email inbox, check for any messages from Embroker regarding quote status and summarize what you find.
3. If you have access to my Embroker account (via browser tool with my configured credentials), check the account dashboard for a quotes/status section and report what's shown — do not submit, accept, or sign anything.
4. Prepare a short checklist for me covering: what to do when quotes arrive (e.g., compare coverage limits/premiums across D&O, E&O, general liability, and cyber), and what to do if the window passes without word (e.g., a draft follow-up message I can send to Embroker asking for a status update).
5. Draft that follow-up message now so it's ready to send if needed.

Done looks like: you've given me the expected delivery window, checked whatever access points are available for status updates, and handed me a ready-to-use checklist plus a drafted follow-up message. Report back with all of this, then stop — waiting for the actual quotes to arrive remains a human step, and I will confirm with you once they land.

ins_001:n5.prompt:
You are helping me compare insurance quotes and produce a recommendation for our startup's D&O, E&O, general liability, and cyber insurance coverage.

First, ask me for the following if not already provided: the quote documents or summaries I've received from each insurance broker/carrier for each of the four coverage types (D&O, E&O, general liability, cyber), including premium amounts, coverage limits, deductibles/retentions, exclusions, and policy terms. If I only have partial quotes (e.g., missing cyber), note that gap explicitly rather than guessing.

Once you have the quote details, do the following:
1. For each coverage type, build a side-by-side comparison table listing: carrier/broker name, annual premium, coverage limit, deductible, key exclusions, and any notable endorsements or conditions.
2. Flag any material differences in exclusions or limits that could leave us underinsured relative to our stage, headcount, funding raised, and industry (ask me for these details if not given, since they affect what's "adequate" coverage).
3. Calculate total annual cost across all four policies for each combination/bundle option if quotes are bundled, and separately if unbundled.
4. Identify the best overall value per coverage type — balancing premium cost against limits and exclusions — and explain the tradeoffs in plain language.
5. Produce a written recommendation memo (one paragraph per coverage type plus a summary) stating which quote to select and why, and note any coverage gaps or negotiation points I should raise with the broker before purchasing.

Done means I have: a comparison table for all four coverage types, a total-cost summary, and a recommendation memo I can review.

Report back with the comparison table, total cost summary, and recommendation memo. Do not purchase, bind, or sign any policy — finalizing and paying for coverage remains a human step.

ins_001:n6.prompt:
You are helping me prepare to select and bind insurance coverage (D&O, E&O, general liability, and cyber) through Embroker. This step ends in a live, legally binding insurance contract, so you must prepare everything but stop short of binding it.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: our company legal name, prior quotes/quote references already obtained from Embroker, our target coverage limits and deductibles for each policy type (D&O, E&O, general liability, cyber), our budget ceiling, desired effective date, and the name/title of the authorized officer who must approve binding.

Then, using my configured credentials, log into the Embroker portal and:
1. Pull up the current quotes for all four coverage lines.
2. Compare limits, deductibles, exclusions, and premiums across the quotes we've received.
3. Draft a clear side-by-side summary comparing coverage terms and total annual cost for each line, flagging any gaps or unusual exclusions.
4. Pre-fill or stage the selections in the Embroker portal (choosing the specific limits/deductibles per my inputs) up to but not including the final bind/confirm action.
5. Prepare a short recommendation memo stating which options you'd bind and why, plus total combined premium.

Do not click bind, accept terms, sign any agreement, or submit payment. This step requires an authorized officer to commit the company financially, so it remains a policy-gate: you must stop for human sign-off before binding.

Report back with: the comparison summary, the staged selections in the portal (with a link or clear description of where they sit), the recommendation memo, and an explicit note that final bind approval is pending sign-off from the named officer.
